children: U.S. natural gas futures post back-to-back losses with the market focusing more on a soft near-term outlook for weather-driven demand than solid LNG exports. Despite some additional cold in overnight forecasts, the weather pattern looks "rather bearish" for the next two weeks, NatGasWeather.com says in a note. Other reasons for selling could include "weather patterns taking on an El El Niño-like set up for late October into November to suggest this winter will in fact play out warmer than normal for lighter than normal demand," the forecaster adds. Nymex natural gas settles down 1.9% at $3.0580/mmBtu.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
